title: Affine calculation for canonical relatively flat module base change
statement: Choose the shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a quasi-compact separated morphism, $g:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $X_B$ the chosen fibre product with projections $p,f_B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $G$ be a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], flat over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Assume tensor pullback along $p$ is additive [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every comparison $c:Lp^*(G[0])\to(p^*G)[0]$ satisfying IsDerivedModulePullbackComparison [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map], the composite of the canonical derived base-change map [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] with $Rf_{B,*}(c)$ is invertible. The functors $L(-)^*$ and $R(-)_*$ are those of [def-pc-derived-pullback] and [def-pc-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Steps 2--5: flat Cech tensor calculation on affine bases; Stacks Tags 0A1D and 08IB

proof.text: Choose the finite alternating affine Cech model for the direct image. Relative flatness makes its modules of sections flat over A; finite products are flat. The bounded flat-complex counit computes derived tensor by ordinary tensor.

Apply the affine sections pullback isomorphism on each intersection; its pure-tensor formula commutes with restrictions and hence differentials. The Cech base-change characterization identifies the resulting isomorphism with the displayed composite. Derived tensor of a degree-zero module has no positive cohomology and has ordinary tensor pullback in degree zero, by a nonpositive flat resolution. Therefore any map from it into the ordinary degree-zero target factors through degree-zero cohomology. Right Kan extension uniqueness relates two left-derived counits by a natural automorphism of derived pullback; this induces an automorphism in degree zero, where changing the counit gives an invertible change of the ordinary pullback; thus its composite differs by an invertible target automorphism.

theorem canonicalModuleBaseChange_isIso_affine_of_isFlatOver
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {A B : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec A)
    [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (g : Spec B ⟶ Spec A)
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).Additive]
    (G : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u} G]
    (hflat : Scheme.Modules.IsFlatOver G f)
    (c : (derivedPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj G) ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (pullback f g).toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj G))
    (hc : IsDerivedModulePullbackComparison (pullback.fst f g) G c) :
    IsIso (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f (pullback.snd f g) g (pullback.fst f g)
        pullback.condition ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj G) ≫
      (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd f g)).map c)
